messages:
Marta Lopez: Quick sync — we need a compact set of differentiators for the launch post and a tiny internal 1-pager for SDRs. Target audience: infra/platform buyers + product engineers evaluating managed LLM APIs. I sketched three candidate claims below, please react with +1 / -1 / edit and add bullets we can ship to design.

Dev Patel: Love the approach. Could we make one claim strictly about "predictable economics" (numbers) and one about "operational continuity" (fallbacks)? keeps it tangible.

Rhea Ng: +1 on both. Also add a line about "same API across hosted/dedicated/private" — that's a big ops win vs multi-vendor glue.

Marta Lopez: Draft claims (verbatim):
1) Predictable inference economics — up to 3x lower per-token cost for production workloads via batching, caching, and runtime-aware routing. (we'll put a benchmark note)
2) One runtime, three modes — same API surface for hosted, reserved, and private deployments so you don't refactor when you scale.
3) Graceful degradation & fallbacks — automatic model routing and tiered capacity to keep apps online during outages or spikes.

Samir Khan: Re: claim 1, can we avoid exact multiplier in public copy unless we have reproducible benchmark doc. Maybe: "meaningfully lower" for the public post, and keep the 3x number in the SDR cheat sheet with a link to the benchmark appendix.

Marta Lopez: Good catch. Public: "meaningfully lower per-token economics on production traffic". Internal: keep the 3x with benchmark link.

LaunchBot: Note created: https://redwood-internal.docs/marketing/launch-differentiators-draft (auto)

Rhea Ng: For SDR 1-pager, we should have quick objection handlers. Examples:
- "Why not use cloud X?" -> "Cloud X ties you to endpoint-per-model; we provide a unified runtime so you can swap models and preserve SLAs."
- "Why not self-host?" -> "Self-host needs ops overhead; Redwood gives the same runtime primitives with optional private deployments and support."

Dev Patel: Webinar angle: "How to get production latency + cost predictability from LLMs" — 30-min technical demo + customer panel. Title options: "Serving-first LLMs: predictable inference at scale" or "From prototype to production: controlling LLM economics". Thoughts?

Marta Lopez: Prefer the second. Add a 5-minute section on routing/fallbacks and a quick graph showing tail-latency improvement after caching.

Samir Khan: For inbound routing: add intent tags to registration form (POC, Enterprise, Research) and route Enterprise leads to AE queue with "Dedicated/Private interest" tag. Quick rule: if they select "SLA/Compliance" + Enterprise -> AE priority.

Rhea Ng: Agree. Also add an addendum for benchmarks in the lead packet: short table with workload type (chat vs summarization), token distribution, and the model variant used.

Marta Lopez: Next steps:
- Dev: polish benchmark appendix and permission to quote the 3x number internally (due EOD tomorrow) — assign to @Dev.
- Samir: inbound routing rules + draft form fields (due EOD Friday).
- Rhea: write SDR objection handlers (first pass by tomorrow AM).
- Design: I'll ping separately for hero alt copy + one-pager layout.

Dev Patel: On it — I'll also attach a tiny reproducibility checklist: seed prompts, seq length distribution, traffic mix.

Samir Khan: I'll prototype the form routing in HubSpot and share the flow.

Marta Lopez: Thanks team :rocket: — if no objections I'll merge these claims into the public launch post draft by noon tomorrow.

LaunchBot: Reminder scheduled: update status in #launch-channel at 1738190000.
